topics.label: Lecture opening and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory welcome and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture before substantive content begins.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address traditional cancer treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux pump resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint losses, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine kinase-driven oncogene addiction, small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the diverse molecular mechanisms and dosing strategies associated with kinase inhibitor resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design, mechanisms of action, and clinical limitations of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and clinical immunotherapies designed to harness or genetically engineer T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Current challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical progress in cancer survival, overarching clinical challenges, and future paradigms in personalized oncology.
